source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Romanian is spelled almost exactly as it sounds, once you know a handful of letters with marks and two c/g rules. It sounds closer to Italian than you might expect.
reading: "uh" is the letter ă, "ts" is ț, and "ch" (as in church) is c before e or i.
A final i is often barely said: faci is "fahch", ești is "yesht".

sounds.name: Ă
sounds.how: The relaxed "uh" in the middle of "sofa". It's never "a" as in "cat".

sounds.name: Â and Î
sounds.how: Two spellings of one sound English doesn't have: say "ee", then pull your tongue back without rounding your lips. A short, throaty "ih" is close enough to be understood.

sounds.name: Ș
sounds.how: sh as in "shoe". The comma underneath is what makes it different from a plain s.

sounds.name: Ț
sounds.how: ts as in "cats", even at the start of a syllable.

sounds.name: Soft and hard C
sounds.how: Before e or i, c is "ch" as in "church": ce = "cheh". Adding an h makes it hard again: che = "keh", chi = "kee". It's the same rule as Italian.

sounds.name: J
sounds.how: zh as in "measure", never the English j.

sounds.name: Gliding vowels
sounds.how: Este, ești and other forms of "to be" start with a y sound: "YES-teh". ea slides to "yah" and oa to "wah".

sounds.name: Whispered final i
sounds.how: After a consonant at the end of a word, i is barely said; it just softens the consonant. Faci is "fahch", ești is "yesht", ocupi is "oh-KOOP".

sounds.name: Rolled R
sounds.how: A quick tap or short trill with the tip of the tongue, as in Spanish or Italian.
